verdicts.reason: Quote states the pin mapping (connectivity); a structural mapping is stated, and checkable from interface signals (o_gpio==cio_gpio_o etc.). Fields fine; keep strength MUST.
Duplicate/description of the same naming mapping as GP-6-01; o_gpio is DATA_OUT and o_gpio_en DATA_OE is just a definition, nothing separate to exercise.

Quote says no pad model/mux exists and i_gpio is driven only by the test bench; this is a design-structure statement, not a per-cycle checkable assertion from interface signals (non-dependence cannot be asserted). Better exercised as a scenario by toggling o_gpio/o_gpio_en and confirming i_gpio is unaffected.

Quote is an informative note that a test following Programmer's Guide examples models the pad itself; it does not say the test must do so. The rule's MUST is invented and the actor 'any' is unfounded.

duplicates.reason: Both come from the same sentence of INT-IO-001 describing the same pin mapping/naming.

questions.question: Programmer's Guide examples assume weak pull-ups on pads while INT-IO-002 says no pad model exists: must the testbench model pads (i_gpio = o_gpio where o_gpio_en=1, else 1) or is any i_gpio stimulus acceptable?
